req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/delete issued by the post's author must delete the post row and redirect to /. We need: (1) a positive test confirming the author can delete their own post and the row is gone + 302 to /; (2) a negative test confirming a non-author gets 403; (3) a boundary test for a non-existent post id (404); plus additional tests for unauthenticated access (401/redirect) and verifying the exact redirect location. Each test uses pre-loaded data: post 2 belongs to user Rahul (id=1), post 7 belongs to user Anjali (id=2). Tests are self-contained with their own app/db setup.

tests.name: test_delete_post_by_author_removes_row_and_redirects
preconditions: Database contains post id=2 authored by Rahul (user id=1)
expected: Subsequent GET / does not contain post title 'Pillow delta willow'
Direct DB query confirms post id=2 no longer exists
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

r_delete = client.post('/2/delete')
assert r_delete.status_code == 302
assert r_delete.headers['Location'] == '/'

r_index = client.get('/')
assert r_index.status_code == 200
assert b'Pillow delta willow' not in r_index.data

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (2,)).fetchone()
    assert row is None

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_delete_post_state_transition_post_gone_after_delete
preconditions: Post id=6 authored by Rahul (user id=1) exists
actions: Verify post id=6 exists via DB query (pre-state)
Verify post id=6 no longer exists via DB query (post-state)
Attempt POST /6/delete again to confirm 404 (terminal state)
expected: Post id=6 absent from DB after first delete
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    pre = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (6,)).fetchone()
    assert pre is not None

r1 = client.post('/6/delete')
assert r1.status_code == 302
assert r1.headers['Location'] == '/'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    post = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (6,)).fetchone()
    assert post is None

r2 = client.post('/6/delete')
assert r2.status_code == 404

os.unlink(path)
